
| Slug | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `agent-work` | An agent from any harness arrives, gets the right task with the credentials and skills it needs, works it, and the session is attributed and priced. |
| `verified-work` | A human can accept work without reading every line, and a bug marked done is actually gone. |
| `org-wide-visibility` | Anyone can see what the whole org is working on, across repos and projects, and find anything in it, without asking a person. |
| `writing-surface` | Anything written down has one home everyone can reach. Filing a note costs nothing. |
| `journalism` | A journalist runs an investigation end to end in Worklode, with no parallel toolchain. |
| `queryable-facts` | Every Worklode object has an IRI that resolves and serves RDF, so a Worklode row and a knowledge-graph node are the same subject. |
| `familiar-surfaces` | An agent does the setup, and every surface behaves the way whoever reaches for it next already expects. |
| `operable-service` | Someone who did not build Worklode can run it and fix it, because the runbook lives in skills. |
| `human-attention` | What actually needs a person is in front of them, and nothing else is. |

One candidate intent, a system that changes itself, is held outside `operable-service` and gated on intents becoming enforceable.
